summary: IDEA000052, IDEA000096, and IDEA000099 remain untested and unselected. GDT769 already covers the relevant role/transition screens; GDT944 supplies the only bounded input/output wording case. No fixed observable discriminator survives within the exposed f77r/f80v/f85r1 packet.
root_review_corrections: GDT944 has three reader cases total: two ZL/IT product bindings and one RF unread product group. No continuation reader default is made live here. Exploratory joint meanings remain permitted without a confirmed anchor; independent repeated bindings are required only for a confirmation or strict contract, not as a prerequisite for hypothesis drafting. The audit therefore states a missing fixed discriminator, without claiming identity is globally absent.

items.title: A transformation preserves material identity while changing state
items.source_example: f80v.32 has `s olkain shol kair or arolkeedy olky qolkain shedy`; f80v.33 continues `qokeedy qoker olkain olshedy ...`, with a later `olshedy` at .36.
items.already_tested: GDT944 explicitly tested formed-versus-separated output (F/S) at .32 and retained the whole continuation: three reader cases total, with two ZL/IT product bindings and RF's product group unread. GDT769 also left liquid/material identity unresolved for ol/ols.
items.genuinely_unknown: The bounded cases do not provide a fixed observable identity-and-state discriminator. A shared input/output conservation hypothesis remains permissible, but the later product mention has no tested identity tie in this packet.
items.credible_rival: A source/content sentence or nominal/field sequence with no conserved material participant explains the same adjacency; the phrase/grammar rival remains viable.
items.distinct_consequence: A conservation reading could predict an input/output identity tie under a predeclared state change, whereas the rival predicts only source/content adjacency. This batch has no fixed observable that separates those predictions.
items.decision: Keep as an explicit hypothesis; do not select or call it a finding.
items.next_smallest_action: Keep both joint hypotheses available for exploratory drafting; if confirmation is later considered, preregister a fixed identity-plus-state observable rather than adding an anchor prerequisite now.

items.title: A transformation preserves an input-output conservation relation
items.source_example: The same f80v.32-to-.36 passage supplies an assumed source `qolkain` and product `shedy`; f85r1.4 has `... doltshdy otar otchdy ols`, but no independently identified input/output pair.
items.already_tested: GDT769's complete local frames include amount, state and process candidates but leave material identity unresolved. GDT944 checked the whole f80v paragraph (three reader cases total; two ZL/IT product bindings and RF unread) and found no fixed identity discriminator. W16 reports no new material-transition interaction.
items.genuinely_unknown: Whether a conserved quantity or participant links a source to an output remains open; the assumed source/product sentence does not decide it, while exploratory shared meanings remain allowed.
items.credible_rival: A transport/continuation or record-field account preserves ordering or state labels without asserting an input-output conservation equation.
items.distinct_consequence: Conservation could predict a repeated participant/quantity relation across an operation; the rival predicts only local adjacency. No fixed observable in this bounded packet separates those predictions.
items.decision: Retain as untested and unselected; no experiment or decoder work is justified.
items.next_smallest_action: Keep the relation as an exploratory hypothesis; a future confirmation would need a predeclared state/quantity observable, with no requirement for a confirmed anchor during exploration.

items.title: A transition marker is direction-neutral continuation rather than an endpoint verb
items.source_example: In exposed f85r1.4, `otar` occurs between `doltshdy` and `otchdy`, followed by `ols` (all RF/ZL/IT variants retain the position).
items.already_tested: GDT769 tested 110 otar occurrences: four clean state bridges ran in mixed directions, including amount-to-next-value, state-to-close/result, and before an independent process. R05 continuation and nominal R01 tied; `bis` remained the identity rival.
items.genuinely_unknown: The pilot occurrence has no independently decoded right-hand attained state, so it cannot separate a neutral continuation marker from an endpoint or nominal field.
items.credible_rival: `bis`/endpoint wording or a preparation/record-field noun remains credible under the same geometry.
items.distinct_consequence: Continuation predicts mixed left/right state directions; endpoint `bis` predicts a repeatedly right-directed attained state. GDT769's mixed-direction result already supplies the available consequence, with no new pilot discriminator.
items.decision: Retain the direction-neutral continuation hypothesis as an exploratory candidate only; do not promote role or identity.
items.next_smallest_action: A future fixed test would need held occurrences with an independently specified right-hand attained-state criterion; do not rerun unchanged GDT769.
